title: 🔄 Complementary Angles — sin and cos are Partners!
hook: Notice how sin 30° = 1/2 = cos 60°? And sin 60° = cos 30°? This isn't coincidence — when two angles add up to 90°, they have a beautiful mirror relationship!
explanation:
Complementary Angles: Two angles are complementary if they add up to 90°. In a right triangle, the two acute angles are always complementary.

The six complementary identities:

IdentityExample
sin(90° − θ) = cos θsin 72° = cos 18°
cos(90° − θ) = sin θcos 55° = sin 35°
tan(90° − θ) = cot θtan 80° = cot 10°
cot(90° − θ) = tan θcot 75° = tan 15°
sec(90° − θ) = cosec θsec 40° = cosec 50°
cosec(90° − θ) = sec θcosec 25° = sec 65°
Why? In a right triangle: the side opposite one acute angle is the side adjacent to the other. So sin of one angle = cos of its complement.
💡 Tip: If you see sin 72°, think: 'That's the same as cos 18°' (since 72° + 18° = 90°).
worked_example:
Example: Evaluate: sin 25° cos 65° + cos 25° sin 65°.

1
Notice complementary pairs
25° + 65° = 90°
2
Apply identities
cos 65° = sin 25° and sin 65° = cos 25°
3
Substitute
sin 25° · sin 25° + cos 25° · cos 25° = sin²25° + cos²25° = 1

try_this.question: Without tables, evaluate: tan 1° · tan 2° · tan 3° · ... · tan 89°.
try_this.hint: Pair: tan 1° with tan 89° = cot 1°. What is tan θ × cot θ?
try_this.answer: tan θ × tan(90°−θ) = tan θ × cot θ = 1 for each pair. Pairs: (1°,89°), (2°,88°), ..., (44°,46°). The middle is tan 45° = 1. Total = 1⁴⁴ × 1 = 1.

fun_fact: The prefix 'co' in cosine literally means 'complement' — cosine is the 'sine of the complement'!
